bullets.title: US economy running hot: PMI, jobs, GDP all beat; inflation re-accelerating
bullets.body: September flash US Composite PMI hit 58.4, highest since July 2021, with manufacturing at 57.0 (est 53.7) and services at 58.7. PSC Macro sees 3Q real GDP tracking at 4%+ with core capex equipment set to grow 20%+, nominal GDP projected at 8.0% q/q ar. Initial jobless claims held below 200k for a second straight week. However, input cost inflation jumped to the highest level since October 2022, raising stagflation risk if Iran conflict sustains energy prices.

bullets.title: Fed signals additional hikes likely; market pricing ~70% Oct hike, 35+ bp through year-end
bullets.body: Fed Governor Barr, Boston Fed Collins, and Chicago Fed Goolsbee all reinforced hawkish messaging last week. Market prediction markets show October hike odds at 66% (up 12% w/w) and December at 70% (up 5% w/w). Morgan Stanley expects two more hikes to 4.25-4.50% held through end-2027. Goolsbee warned 'restoring price stability won't be painless' and raised concerns that demand may be contributing to inflation alongside energy and tariffs. The 2-year yield approached 5.22% resistance with potential curve inversion risk into early 2027.

bullets.title: Oil -4-5% on Iran diplomacy hopes, Saudi pipeline restart; diesel at record $6.51/gal
bullets.body: Brent crude fell to $99-100/bbl (largest four-day decline in over a year) as Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West Pipeline and Iranian officials proposed Hormuz reopening within 7 days if the U.S. lifts port blockades. Iran's conditions include asset releases and ceasefire across all fronts. Separately, US diesel prices hit a record $6.51/gallon amid Russian refinery damage and tight domestic refining capacity; Republican lawmakers and Treasury Secretary Bessent examined feasibility of a diesel export ban.

bullets.title: Treasury yields at post-2007 highs; 5Y auction tailed badly; curve flattening signals macro risk
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.10-5.17% during the week while the 5-year auction tailed 3.1-3.2bp with end-user demand at multi-year lows. JPMorgan raised its YE26 2-year target to 4.70% and 10-year to 5.05%. The 2s-10s curve compressed to ~19bp, the flattest since early 2022. Morgan Stanley raised 2H26 Brent oil and JPMorgan raised near-term oil forecasts to $95/bbl, citing persistent Middle East disruptions.

bullets.title: Agentic AI inflection: META Muse tops App Store, drives CPU/memory rally; AMZN blocks agent
bullets.body: Meta's Muse AI personal agent launched September 8 and within 13 days reached 2.5-3.1M downloads, outpacing ChatGPT's comparable launch metrics. Muse hit #1 in the US/Canada App Store and added Shopify, PayPal, Expedia, Instacart, and Walmart as connector partners. Amazon blocked Muse citing unauthorized access and credential concerns. META shares surged 11-12% (best day in 17+ months). The agentic AI theme drove a sharp semiconductor rotation: AMD hit $1T market cap (+9-10%), INTC +12-14%, and ARM +17% as markets re-priced CPU/memory demand (agents require 3-4 GPUs per CPU versus 7-8 for training).

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex ROI debate: $300B annual AI revenue needed to justify $800B+ 2026 spend
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs calculates hyperscalers need ~$11.6bn per GW/year (~$300B annually industry-wide) to hit 15% ROIC on 2026-27 capex. Cloud backlogs at AWS, Azure, GCP total ~$1.69T (+152% YoY), providing confidence on monetization. Consensus now assumes $800B in 2026 and $1.1T in 2027, but capex growth is expected to decelerate materially from 93% YoY this year toward 61% in 2027 and 14% in 2028. The debate has shifted from whether capex is justified to what monetization level is required to sustain returns.

bullets.title: AI financing risks elevated: circular leverage, Oracle force majeure, SoftBank $11B junk bond
bullets.body: Oracle invoked force majeure on its 2.45GW Project Jupiter New Mexico data center, citing gas pipeline permitting delays until 2027. The project debt traded below 90 cents. SoftBank raised $11.1B in junk bonds at 8.625-9.75% yields, drawing $20B+ in demand. Wolfe Research/BIS highlighted circular AI financing structures: AI companies, chipmakers, and infrastructure providers are interconnected through debt, and a slowdown could trigger contagion. The Wolfe AI Financing Gap webcast covered leveraged buildout risks.

bullets.title: US-China trade truce likely extended 3-6 months; Trump-Xi summit light on major deals
bullets.body: USTR Greer indicated a 3-6 month trade truce extension is possible, and US proposed extending the current truce to January 10 at the Trump-Xi summit. Xi is visiting Sept 23-25 but unlikely to bring a CEO delegation. Discussions covered AI safety (new 'hotline' or 'incident line' agreed), semiconductor restrictions, rare earth controls, and trade. WSJ reported Xi pressed Trump on halting Taiwan arms sales, but no grand bargain materialized. A follow-up meeting in Shenzhen in two months on AI was announced.

bullets.title: Small caps underperforming sharply: Russell 2000 in -6.8% to -7.6% drawdown; breadth deteriorating
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 drew down 6.8-7.6% from cycle peak, with over 70% of SPX constituents in -10%+ drawdowns from 52-week highs. New 52-week lows outpaced highs on the NYSE for 17 consecutive days. S&P 500 equal-weight underperformed cap-weight by ~130bp on the best days. JPMorgan noted only 30% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day MAs despite the index near ATH. The Nasdaq registered 18+ consecutive days of more new lows than highs before the AI-driven reversal.

bullets.title: ECB may hike faster than expected: Eurozone PMI surges to 53.1, headline CPI to rise to 3.6%
bullets.body: The Eurozone September composite PMI rose 1.0pt to 53.1, consistent with 1.7% annualized GDP growth and ahead of all forecasts. JPMorgan noted this is above its 4Q26 forecast of 1.5% and consistent with 5-6 total ECB hikes; the latest PMI could push to six. Headline HICP is expected to jump 0.4pt to 3.6% YoY next week. Services PMI rebounded; input prices rose 3.7pts to 66.5. UK wages projected at ~3.5% in 2027, above BoE's 3.1% target, suggesting the BoE will also need to hike more.

bullets.title: WBD merger clears final hurdle: Paramount antitrust settlement with state AGs expected to close in ~2 weeks
bullets.body: Paramount Skydance reached a settlement with a coalition of state AGs resolving the Warner Bros. Discovery antitrust lawsuit. Terms include 30-32 theatrical films/year (penalties of $30M per missed film), $1.5B in incremental US production spend over 5 years, $47.5M workforce development fund, and an independent compliance monitor. No structural divestitures required. The deal avoids a $7M/day ticking fee starting October 1 and could close within two weeks. Morgan Stanley raised PSKY PT to $11.50.

bullets.title: Semis rotation: SOX +5.5% w/w, but breadth narrow; CPU/optical outperform on agentic AI theme
bullets.body: The SOX gained 5.5% for the week with ALAB +44%, ARM +39%, CRDO +28%, INTC/AMD +25% leading on agentic AI CPU demand re-pricing. MU rallied on memory undersupply narrative (DRAM fulfillment ~60%, HBM shortage persisting). However, breadth was narrow; one-third of semi names remained down 30%+ from highs. Optical names (CIEN, LITE, COHR) rallied on ECOC conference takeaways showing accelerating 1.6T ramp and NPO adoption. CIEN was upgraded to Outperform at Evercore ISI with $550 PT (from $375).

bullets.title: SaaS/software YTD underperformance vs AI enablers: IGV -1.2% vs S&P 500 +12.6%
bullets.body: The Wolfe All-SaaS index trades at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales, with IGV returning -1.2% YTD vs S&P +12.6%. Security software outperformed (+36.5% YTD per Citi) as agentic AI created demand for AI-native security, but broader software names face margin headwinds from AI inference costs. Morgan Stanley's AI mapping shows software adopters have seen 460bp EBIT margin expansion in 2025-26, but median forward P/E has reset to 18x (vs 22x for enablers). The AI trade is shifting toward a barbell of select enablers plus emerging adopters.

bullets.title: Cable/telecom disruption risk from AI agents: CMCSA downgraded; TMUS most insulated
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgraded CMCSA to Underweight ($18 PT) citing broadband net add deterioration (-558K 2026 estimate vs consensus -509K) as fiber, FWA, and Starlink compete. Morgan Stanley cut CMCSA PT to $27 and CHTR to $140, noting cable operators face greater AI agent-driven ARPU risk than telcos. BNP Paribas noted agentic AI can negotiate bills and switch providers, threatening 'consumer inertia.' TMUS is the most insulated: 60% of new accounts select premium plans, reducing switching incentives. AT&T raised to Outperform at BNP with $30 PT on fiber convergence.

bullets.title: Consumer spending resilient but bifurcated; gasoline and diesel costs creating strain for lower-income
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Consumer Cash Pile reached $22.62T in 2Q26 with all income brackets except the bottom 20th percentile holding 6-27% more real cash than 2019. However, gas prices at $4.61 and diesel at $6.51 are having incrementally larger negative impact on lower-income households (threshold sensitivity $3.70 vs $4.02 for higher-income). UBS softlines September survey showed lower-income Happiness Score declined 3.2 points MoM. Real consumption growth is expected to slow to 1.8% (4Q/4Q) in 2027 from 2.2% in 2026.

bullets.title: El Niño risk: 2026-27 Super El Niño could be strongest on record with $3.1T cumulative economic losses
bullets.body: Jefferies assembled nearly 50 analysts covering 150+ stocks exposed to the 2026-27 Super El Niño, forecasted as the strongest in modern history with contemporaneous losses at 0.6% of global GDP and cumulative $3.1T over five years. Key risks: food inflation via crop disruption (rice, wheat, sugar, palm oil), water stress at Panama Canal/Rhine/Danube, hydropower constraints, and labor productivity losses from extreme heat. Peak food inflation impact expected in H1 2027. Geopolitical disruptions from Iran and Ukraine reduce global food system resilience.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Democrats projected to retake House (90% odds), Senate toss-up; energy/AI policy at stake
bullets.body: JPMorgan put Democratic House flip odds at 90% with Senate a toss-up. Rising fuel prices (~30% higher gasoline) are the defining voter issue, particularly in the Midwest. Morgan Stanley noted Republicans winning would favor AI power infrastructure and defense spending; Democratic sweep would favor SNAP-exposed retailers and Medicaid stocks. State elections are critical for AI data center permitting in Texas, Virginia, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. Post-midterm Congress faces debt ceiling risks as early as late winter 2027.

bullets.title: Texas halts data center permits; regulatory pushback broadening across US and EU
bullets.body: Texas Governor Abbott ordered TCEQ to halt all new data center environmental permits pending ERCOT/PUCT/water audits with a decision expected October 19. Governor is also moving to eliminate data center incentives. California enacted an oversight package requiring electricity, water, and local disclosure. LA County, Bay Area municipalities, Chicago, and Dallas are all considering moratoriums. Jefferies estimated 45 delayed/blocked US projects worth $68B. Prince William County reduced by-right data center overlay by 62%, requiring special use permits.

bullets.title: AKAM-Anthropic $11.6B deal validates distributed CPU-based AI cloud; transforms earnings story
bullets.body: Akamai announced a 7-year $11.6B take-or-pay contract with Anthropic for CPU-based distributed cloud infrastructure, expandable to $20B. The deal requires $5.5B capex, implies ~$1.7B annual revenue at full run-rate by end-2028, and features $22M/MW economics. AKAM surged 15-23% on the announcement. Multiple analysts raised price targets (Oppenheimer $180, D.A. Davidson $185, JPM $167). The deal validates distributed CPU-based architecture for frontier AI and could attract additional large customer wins beyond the current 93% Anthropic concentration.

bullets.title: Brazil/LatAm macro: Argentina GDP worst since COVID; Brazil growth forecast cut to +1.5% in 2026
bullets.body: JPMorgan cut Argentina's 2026 growth forecast to 1.5% YoY after July activity contracted 2.9% MoM, the worst since April 2020. Manufacturing fell 3.6% and construction 4.0% in July. Brazil's Finance Ministry cut its 2026 GDP forecast to 2.0% from 2.3%, and BCB Copom minutes signaled a pause at 13.75% through year-end. BofA expects back-to-back 25bp Selic cuts through December 2027. Colombia upgraded external debt to OW at BofA. Banxico unanimously held at 6.50% and is expected on hold through mid-2027.
